messages:
leah_customer_netops: Hi team — we're seeing mTLS handshake failures to our Redwood Private control plane since this morning after a firewall policy push. Client logs show 'TLSv1.3 alert handshake_failure (40)'. Using control plane FQDN cp-us-east-1.controlplane.redwood. Any pointers?

amanda_support: thanks @leah_customer_netops — can you paste the exact error text and whether you're resolving the FQDN or hitting an IP? Also are you behind a corporate NGFW that does TLS inspection?

leah_customer_netops: resolving FQDN. Exact: "TLSv1.3 alert handshake_failure (40)" and connection closed immediately. No request-id header on logs. We can repro with curl and our client cert.

raj_netops: we rolled out an outbound SSL inspection rule yesterday (BlueCoat profile) that may re-sign certs. Could be related.

amanda_support: ok please run these checks and paste outputs: 1) openssl s_client -connect cp-us-east-1.controlplane.redwood:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -state -msg -debug 2) tcpdump -n -s 0 -w capture.pcap 'tcp port 443 and host <controlplane-ip>' capturing initial handshake.

leah_customer_netops: attaching redacted snippets from openssl/tcpdump: 

-----BEGIN SNIPPET-----
> ClientHello, TLSv1.3, Cipher Suites: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
> extension: server_name (len=...) "cp-us-east-1.controlplane.redwood"
< TLSv1.2 Alert, length 2
0000: 15 03 03 00 02 00 28  ... (alert handshake_failure)
-----END SNIPPET-----

openssl s_client summary: connection aborted, SSL alert number 40, no server cert presented to client.

jordan_eng: tagging eng-infra. On our side control-plane ingress logs show TLS alert 40 from the client IP and 'no shared ciphers' near the handshake. Two leading hypotheses: 1) NGFW is acting as an intercepting TLS proxy and not forwarding client certs (so mutual TLS fails), 2) the proxy/middlebox strips or rewrites ClientHello extensions (SNI/ALPN/cipher list) leaving no usable cipher.

amanda_support: important note: mutual TLS requires the original client cert to reach the server. If your NGFW terminates TLS and reopens a separate TLS session to us, it will not forward the client cert. For mTLS you need TLS passthrough or explicit bypass for the control plane endpoints.

raj_netops: the NGFW does re-sign by default. We can add exceptions. What endpoints/IPs should we whitelist?

amanda_support: please whitelist the control plane FQDN cp-us-east-1.controlplane.redwood and these example egress IPs used by the control plane: 34.210.11.5, 34.210.11.6 (confirm exact IPs from your support contact). Also ensure the NGFW preserves SNI and ALPN and does not perform TCP MSS clamping that fragments ClientHello. If you cannot bypass inspection, configure the NGFW to do TLS passthrough for that FQDN.

jordan_eng: another debug hint: in tcpdump we saw a truncated ClientHello where the certificate_request extension was missing from the server handshake path. That points to an in-path device altering the ClientHello bytes (inspection or segmentation).

leah_customer_netops: we added an inspection bypass for the FQDN and disabled re-sign for the control plane traffic. Retried with curl using our client cert — handshake now completes and requests authenticate successfully.

amanda_support: great — please monitor for a few hours. We'll document this as a KB: 'Corporate TLS inspection will break Redwood Private mTLS — bypass control plane FQDNs or enable passthrough.'

controlplane-bot: created ticket RED-10234 to update docs and platform onboarding checklist.

raj_netops: we'll roll the bypass config to all regions this week.

leah_customer_netops: confirmed stable for 6h and counting. Thanks for the quick help.

amanda_support: closing in 24h if stable. :thumbsup:
